topics.title: Cut or scrape
steps: Wash your hands or put on gloves.
Press on the cut with a clean dressing until it stops bleeding.
Rinse the wound with clean water and pat it dry.
Cover it with a sterile dressing or plaster, and change it daily.
getHelp: It's still bleeding after 10 minutes of firm pressure
The cut is deep or gaping, or something is stuck in it
It turns red, hot, swollen or oozes pus, or you get a fever

topics.title: Nosebleed
steps: Lean forward (don't tip your head back) and breathe through your mouth.
Pinch the soft part of your nose for 10 to 15 minutes without letting go.
Hold gauze under your nose to catch blood.
Avoid blowing your nose for a few hours afterwards.
getHelp: It lasts longer than 20 minutes
It started after a head injury
It keeps coming back

topics.title: Burn
steps: Cool the burn under cool (not ice-cold) water, or hold a cool, wet compress on it, for 20 minutes.
Take off rings or tight items near the burn before it swells.
Cover it loosely with cling film or a clean, non-fluffy dressing.
getHelp: The burn is bigger than your palm
It's on the face, hands, feet, joints or genitals
It's from chemicals or electricity
The skin looks white, leathery or charred

topics.title: Sprain or strain
steps: Rest the injured part and stop the activity that hurt it.
Hold a cold pack wrapped in a cloth on it for up to 20 minutes, every 2 to 3 hours.
Wrap it with a compression bandage, firm but not tight.
Raise it above heart level when you can.
getHelp: You can't move it or put any load on it
It looks bent or out of shape
It feels numb or tingly, or turns pale or blue
It isn't better after a few days

topics.title: Fall, tumble or collision
steps: Stop, anchor yourself, and take a few slow breaths.
Check yourself from head to toe: head, neck, back, shoulders, wrists, hips, knees and ankles. Note anything that hurts or won't move normally.
Hold a cold pack wrapped in a cloth on any sore spot for up to 20 minutes.
Rest for a while, and tell a crewmate what happened so someone keeps an eye on you.
Tell me what hurts, for example "my wrist hurts", and I'll give you the steps for it.
getHelp: You hit your head, or feel confused, sick or drowsy afterwards
Your neck or back hurts, or you have numbness or tingling
You can't move a joint or put load on it, or it looks out of shape

topics.title: Bruise or bump
steps: Hold a cold pack wrapped in a cloth on it for up to 20 minutes.
Rest the area.
Repeat the cold pack a few times a day for the first 2 days.
getHelp: The swelling is large or keeps growing
The pain is severe, or you can't move the area
It was a hit to the head (see Head injury)

topics.title: Headache
steps: Check the cabin CO2 reading. A CO2 rise is a common cause of headaches on a spacecraft.
Drink water. Fluid shift means you may not feel thirsty.
Rest somewhere quiet and dim, away from screens.
Use pain relief from the medical kit only as the flight surgeon directs.
getHelp: It comes on suddenly and is the worst you've had
You also have vision changes, confusion, weakness or a stiff neck
It follows a hit to the head
It lasts more than a day

topics.title: Nausea or space motion sickness
steps: Keep your head still and avoid quick head movements.
Fix your eyes on a stable point. Keep a consistent 'up' in the module.
Take small sips of water often.
getHelp: You can't keep fluids down for 24 hours
There's blood in the vomit
You have severe stomach pain or signs of dehydration

topics.title: Upset stomach or diarrhoea
steps: Rest, and sip water or oral rehydration salts from the kit often, a little at a time.
Clean your hands carefully after every toilet visit, and clean the toilet area after use.
Don't prepare or share food for the crew until you're better.
Eat small, plain meals when you feel ready.
getHelp: It lasts more than 24 hours, or you can't keep fluids down
There's blood in your stool or vomit
You have a fever or severe stomach pain
Other crew members get the same symptoms

topics.title: Back pain
steps: Gently pull your knees toward your chest and hold it, which eases the spine.
Do gentle stretches, and keep up your exercise routine.
Use a heat pack on the sore area for 15 to 20 minutes.
getHelp: You have numbness or weakness in your legs
You lose bladder or bowel control
It follows a fall or a hit
It keeps getting worse

topics.title: Something in the eye
steps: Don't rub it.
Blink several times, then flush the eye with clean water or the eyewash from the kit.
Wear eye protection when particles may be floating.
getHelp: A chemical got in it: flush for 20 minutes, then get help
Your vision changes
The pain or redness doesn't go away after flushing

topics.title: Dehydration
steps: Drink water steadily, a little at a time.
Use oral rehydration salts from the medical kit if you have them.
Check your urine colour: 1 to 3 on the chart is good, 4 to 5 is watch, 6 to 8 means act.
Log your water intake in VITALS (green range: 2.5 to 3.5 litres a day).
getHelp: You're confused, very dizzy or faint
Your urine is very dark (6 to 8 on the chart), or you aren't passing urine

topics.title: Dizziness or light-headedness
steps: Stop and anchor yourself so you can't drift into anything.
Drink some water.
Check your heart rate and SpO2 in VITALS.
Move slowly for a while.
getHelp: You faint
You also have chest pain or trouble breathing
It keeps coming back

topics.title: Poor sleep or tiredness
steps: Keep a regular sleep schedule, even on busy days.
Dim the lights before sleep and use an eye mask and earplugs.
Avoid caffeine in the 6 hours before sleep.
Secure your sleeping bag so you don't drift.
getHelp: You're under 6 hours a night for several nights
Tiredness affects your work or safety

topics.title: Fever or feeling unwell
steps: Rest and drink plenty of fluids.
Check your temperature in VITALS (green range: 36.1 to 37.2 °C).
Keep away from crewmates where you can, and clean shared surfaces.
getHelp: Your temperature goes above 38.0 °C
It lasts more than 2 days
You also have trouble breathing or chest pain

topics.title: Rash, itch or dry skin
steps: Clean the area gently with a no-rinse cleanser and pat it dry.
Use a moisturiser from the kit.
Try not to scratch. A cold compress helps with itching.
getHelp: The rash spreads fast or blisters
You also have a fever
Your face, lips or throat swell (emergency)

topics.title: Muscle cramp
steps: Gently stretch the muscle and hold the stretch.
Massage the area.
Drink some water.
getHelp: Cramps keep coming back
There is swelling, redness or ongoing pain in the leg

topics.title: Toothache
steps: Rinse your mouth with warm salt water if you have it, or clean water.
Hold a cold pack on the outside of your cheek.
Use pain relief from the medical kit only as the flight surgeon directs.
getHelp: Your face or jaw swells
You have a fever
The pain is severe or lasts more than a day
